newsitem.title: USA: Stocks brace for Federal Reserve's meeting.
newsitem.headline: Stocks brace for Federal Reserve's meeting.

text.p: Wall Street stocks fell Monday on stiff selling as investors worried anew about Tuesday's meeting of the Federal Reserve's interest-rate-setting group.
At 1 p.m. EDT, the Dow Jones industrial average was off 32.19 points to 5,856.27 after bouncing back from a loss of more than 50 points.
In the broader market, declining issues beat advances 3-1 on light volume of 160 million shares on the New York Stock Exchange.
"The market is very jumpy in anticipation of the Fed, said Graham Tanaka, president of Tanaka Capital Management.

"It would be healthy if the Fed raised rates by 25 basis points (one quarter percentage point) which would address the criticism the Fed is playing politics," Tanaka said. "It wouldn't do a whole lot for the economy, but it may help on the emotion side."

The central bank's policy-setting Federal Open Market Committee meets Tuesday and the speculation is that it could bump up short-term interest rates by one quarter or one half of a percentage point to ward off inflationary pressures.
But there is also the possibility that the FOMC may do nothing, and leave interest rates unchanged ahead of the November elections.

"If there was a 25 basis point rise, the market will go up (on relief that the hike wasn't bigger) and if there's no increase, the market will be wishy-washy," said Thom Brown, a managing director of Rutherford Brown & Catherwood.
He said he expected no change in monetary policy and saw very slim chances of a one-half of a percentage point hike.
"The market looks pretty shaky but it's really the nervous professionals that are selling," Brown said.
Wall Street is concerned that higher interest rates could slow corporate profits and dampen consumer spending.
In the bond market, the 30-year Treasury bond was off 5/32, raising its yield to 7.06 percent from 7.04 percent at Friday's close.
Meanwhile, the technology-laden Nasdaq Composite index was off 9.65 at 1,210.04.
The Nasdaq index has recently outperformed the Dow Jones index due to optimism about the tech sector.
Among special situations, Mossimo, the apparel designer that went public in February, tumbled 13-7/8 to 27-1/4 after it warned that its third-quarter earnings would fall far short of expectations.

Diamond Shamrock lost 1/2 to 29-3/4 and Ultramar Corp. added 1/4 to 28-3/4 after the companies agreed to a merger in which each share of Diamond Shamrock will be converted into 1.02 shares of Ultramar in a deal worth $858 million.

Lehman Brothers, whose stock gained Friday on takeover speculation, added 1/2 to 23-1/4. The brokerage house said it knew of no business reason to account for the unusual activity. It also declined to confirm or deny if it was a possible takeover candidate.
Late last week, Business Week magazine said Lehman was a possible takeover candidate and cited an unidentified banker as saying the firm was actively in talks.
Alcoa lost 1-1/2 to 59 and Alumax was off 3/4 to 32-3/8. Goldman cut the stocks to market perform from outperform.
Exide Electronics climbed 2-7/8 to 12 on news that it won an Air Force contract with a potential value of $625 million to provide and service power supply systems.
The American Stock Exchange index was off 1.65 points at 563.55.
